description:
372 tiles at 16x16 for a village fair on a green, in daylight: trodden paths, straw round the stalls, a plank stage and big striped marquees, with bell tents, market stalls, a carousel whose roof and horses turn, a high striker, a coconut shy and bunting to string between its poles. Commercial use permitted, in unlimited projects, with no attribution required; the one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the pack itself.

Importers for RPG Maker MZ, Tiled and Godot ship in the download, and each was run by the engine it targets and made to count what it built.

What is in the download

  • 235 of the 372 tiles are transitions, 63% of the pack. 5 complete 47-mask autotile sets: every inner corner, outer corner, edge, junction and single. Completeness is checked mechanically on every build, because a set missing three tiles is broken in your map.
  • A marquee you paint to any shape. The striped canvas is a faced set: paint the roof as a mass on the green and its south wall draws itself, the stripes running on down the canvas. Every marquee tile is declared blocked in tiles.json, because a tent is walked round.
  • A stage you can walk onto. The plank stage is a faced set too, with a board front and a lit nosing, and every stage tile is walkable: it is a step, not a wall.
  • Paths and straw. The trodden paths and the straw spread on the green and on the paths each have their own set with a soft organic edge.
  • 5 materials × 4 variants, the three walking grounds on a value ladder laid out before any art existed, so a path, a lawn and a straw yard never merge into one muddy field. The smallest gap on the ladder is 21.7 luma, measured from the shipped pixels rather than declared.
  • 20 objects across 53 prop tiles plus the animation frames: bell tents in red and in blue stripes, market stalls under red, blue and yellow awnings (each stocked in a colour its awning is not), a high striker, a coconut shy, a cake table, a picnic table, a hay bale, a barrel, a crate of apples, a tub of flowers, an A-board with an arrow, a bunting pole and the bunting. Each ships transparent, and grounded on its floor with the contact shadow drawn.
  • 4 animated objects, 64 frames: a carousel whose striped roof and eight horses turn together and loop exactly, a flag that waves, a paper lantern that sways and flickers, and a bunch of balloons each bobbing on its own beat. No two frames of a set are the same picture.
  • A finished 40x28 sample map with 122 objects on it and every autotile set placed, as a PNG, as JSON naming every cell by tile id, and as a .tmx that opens in Tiled.
  • 20 4x4 proof renders, one per repeating tile, so you can look for the grid line yourself.
  • Every tile as a loose PNG and as packed sheets: 443 files in total, and a tiles.json giving every tile's role, material, sheet slot, footprint and passability.

Three things to know before you buy

⚠️ A peaked tent is an object; a marquee is a set. A 47-shape autotile takes any outline you paint but cannot carry a ridge, so the big marquee is a striped roof you paint to any shape and the bell tents are placed objects with their peak, door and guy ropes drawn. There are no people or animals in the pack.

⚠️ The animation plays in Tiled and Godot, not in RPG Maker MZ. MZ animates tiles only through its A1 page, which holds animated water autotiles; this pack has none, so in MZ the carousel, the flag, the lantern and the balloons arrive as static frames on pages C and D.

⚠️ At 372 tiles it is a smaller pack than most of the series, and it is priced for that.

The importers were actually run

  • RPG Maker MZ: an A2 autotile sheet (the page MZ's own autotile brush paints) plus B/C/D object pages and a slot map. It composes correctly against MZ's own FLOOR_AUTOTILE_TABLE: 5 of 5 sets, 235 of 235 masked tiles, and 240 of 240 shapes came back byte-identical. The object pages carry every fill, every object and every animation frame.
  • Tiled: one .tsx per group, all 9 opened and rendered by Tiled 1.12.2's own tmxrasterizer and compared pixel for pixel with the shipped sheets: 620 sheet cells, 0 differing. The sample map's .tmx renders 1,146,880 pixels identical to the shipped PNG.
  • Godot 4: a .tres TileSet, loaded and verified in Godot 4.7.2: 9 atlas sources, 372 of 372 declared tiles built, 94 of 94 multi-cell footprints exact. Every sheet is referenced by a relative filename, so the folder loads from wherever you put it in a project.

What is proven, and what is not

The grid is exact, the palette is locked to 44 colours, the alpha is strictly binary with no anti-aliasing, every tile carries a declared role, and every autotile set is complete: exact checks, run on every build.

Seamlessness is not on that list. Every tile's wrap boundary is measured against its own interior, and every 4x4 repetition is rendered and reviewed; grid, palette and autotile completeness are machine-proven. The renders ship with the pack so you can judge them yourself.

The autotile sets

  • trodden_on_green
  • straw_on_green
  • straw_on_trodden
  • boards_on_green
  • marquee_on_green

It fits the rest of the series

The 16x16 Verdant packs are drawn at one cell size in one style, so this fair sits beside the others and a map can run straight out of it into another pack.

  • Verdant 09 — Town — the town the fair comes to: its market, housefronts and gardens
  • Verdant 13 — Castle — the curtain wall, keep and gatehouse whose green the fair sets up on
  • Verdant 01 — Overworld — the fields and roads around it, on the same grid

AI disclosure

Tagged as AI-assisted. Precisely: every tile is drawn by a procedural generator written for this series, and that generator's code was written with AI assistance. No diffusion model is anywhere in the tile pipeline. Every image on this page, the cover included, is composed from the pack's own tiles and sample map.
